newsitem.title: USA: EU's Brittan denies Europe "gone soft" on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan denies Europe "gone soft" on Cuba.

text.p: European Union trade commissioner Leon Brittan denied that the EU has "gone soft" on Cuba, despite its opposition to U.S. penalties for doing business with Cuba.
Brittan, speaking to the European-American Chamber of Commerce, reiterated his opposition to the Helms-Burton Act, signed by President Bill Clinton last July.
"We believe in constructive engagement as the best way of bringing Cuba in from the cold and getting her to behave as a responsible member of the international community," Brittan said.
While noting that current EU initiatives promoting human rights and a free press in Cuba mirror the goals of the Helms-Burton Act, Brittan insisted the U.S. has no right to dictate European action.

"Europe will not act under duress. But fortunately the policy that we have arrived at independently and will pursue independently has the same objective as that of the U.S., even if we pursue it by different means," Brittan said.
